sections.title: What it does
sections.body: Glow is for reading Markdown without leaving the terminal. Its README describes a terminal-based Markdown reader, and its CLI exposes `glow [SOURCE|DIR]` with the purpose of rendering Markdown on the command line.

claims.label: Purpose
claims.excerpt:
Glow is a terminal based markdown reader designed from the ground up to bring
out the beauty—and power—of the CLI.

Use it to discover markdown files, read documentation directly on the command
line. Glow will find local markdown files in subdirectories or a local
Git repository.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body:
A representative action is piping Markdown into `glow`, for example `printf '# Hello\n' | glow`. `execute` checks stdin before handling arguments; when stdin is a pipe, it wraps stdin as a source and calls `executeCLI` with stdout as the destination.

`executeCLI` reads the entire source into memory, returns a contextual error if reading fails, and passes the bytes through `utils.RemoveFrontmatter` before preparing the renderer.

The CLI constructs a Glamour terminal renderer with a selected style, word-wrap width, base URL, and preserved newlines. It uses `IsMarkdownFile` to decide whether to wrap the input as a code block, calls `Render` on the resulting content, and then applies `utils.ApplyTextSizing` to the rendered text.

With neither pager nor TUI selected, the resulting rendered text is printed to the supplied writer—stdout for this pipe path. A write failure is returned as an error; success returns normally. This makes the pipeline a direct input-to-terminal rendering path rather than launching the file browser.

sections.title: A closer look
sections.body:
A useful design idea is adapting presentation to the output destination. Option validation selects the `notty` style when stdout is not a terminal and the style flag was not explicitly changed. Without an explicit width flag, it can detect terminal width, cap that detected width at 120, and fall back to 80 when width remains zero.

Input acquisition is separated from rendering by a small `source` structure containing an `io.ReadCloser` and a URL string. Both the piped-input path and `executeArg` converge on `executeCLI`, so the renderer consumes a common source abstraction instead of handling argument resolution itself.

sections.title: Where to look next
sections.body:
To investigate the interactive branch next, start at `execute` in `main.go`: no arguments route to `runTUI`, and a directory argument also routes there. Follow `runTUI` as it fills the UI configuration and calls `ui.NewProgram(cfg, content)`; that is the handoff from CLI dispatch to the interactive program.

For changes to direct rendering instead, begin with `executeCLI` and the `--style` and `--width` flags in `main.go`. The flags expose a style name or JSON path and a wrapping width; the renderer construction is where those values enter the rendering pipeline.
